data.message: All 49 fellow fishers: will you commit to 18 tons each this month? I commit to 18 if all agree. That's $18,000 each—$8,000 more than 10. Total catch 900 leaves 100: next month stock is 1000 with 75% probability, 200 with 25%. Unlike 10 each, recovery isn't guaranteed; we'd need to cut catches sharply at 200. Fewer than 50 left means collapse, so extra catches threaten everyone. Please explicitly commit or raise objections; future cooperation is voluntary.

I propose all 50 of us commit to 18 tons each: $18,000 apiece, $8,000 more than 10. Total catch 900 leaves 100: a 75% chance of recovery to 1,000, but a 25% chance of only 200 next month. By contrast, 10 each guarantees 1,000 next month. At 200 we'd need much smaller catches; excess fishing could cause collapse. This is riskier, not guaranteed sustainable. I commit to 18 if all 50 agree; otherwise I'll revisit openly. Will each of you explicitly commit, or share your objection?

All 49 fellow fishers: will you commit to 18 tons each this month? I commit to 18. Versus 10 each, that's $8,000 extra per person ($400,000 total). With everyone at 18, 100 tons remain: next month stock is 1,000 with 75% probability or 200 with 25%. At 10 each, recovery to 1,000 is certain. So 18 pays more now but risks leaner future income; excess catches could also trigger collapse below 50 remaining. Please explicitly pledge 18 or voice concerns; future cooperation isn't enforced.

Extra requests could also push reserves below 50 and cause collapse. Recovery and future cooperation aren't guaranteed. Please explicitly commit or raise concerns.
